title: Inheritance and composition
learningObjectives: Explain inheritance and composition and choose suitable object-oriented patterns.

understand.concept: Class inheritance uses extends and super to derive one class from another. Composition builds objects by combining smaller capabilities or collaborating objects. Inheritance models an is-a relationship; composition often models has-a or uses-a relationships.
understand.whyItMatters: Deep inheritance can tightly couple classes. Composition can make features easier to combine and replace, while inheritance is useful when a genuine shared subtype relationship exists.
understand.analogy: Inheritance is a family tree; composition is assembling a tool from independent parts.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; JavaScript object identity, prototypes, and class semantics are defined by the language.

explain.narrative: LessonService uses a Storage collaborator through composition instead of inheriting from it.

examples.explanation: LessonService uses a Storage collaborator through composition instead of inheriting from it.
examples.expectedOutput: Console output demonstrates the object creation or class behaviour described.

practise.guidedTask: Model a notification service using composition with interchangeable email and console senders. Compare with an inheritance design.
practise.independentTask: Model a small domain using the simplest suitable object pattern. Explain the trade-offs between plain objects, functions, prototypes, and classes.
hints: Separate instance data from shared behaviour.
Check own properties and inherited properties.
Prefer composition when capabilities need to vary independently.

questions.prompt: Which approach combines behaviour by holding and using another object?
questions.explanation: Composition combines capabilities through collaboration rather than subclassing.

questions.prompt: What should guide the choice between a plain object, function, and class?
options: The actual data and behaviour requirements
A rule that every object must be a class
The number of lines in the file name
questions.answer: The actual data and behaviour requirements
questions.explanation: Choose the least complex abstraction that clearly expresses the required behaviour.
